## What happened pm-changelog 2026.11.7 changed how entries inside a section are ordered. #324 (merged 2026-11-06) switched `compareItems` from the old item timestamp to the SDK's `resolveCompletionTimestamp`, so `completed_at` now wins over `closed_at`. The new order is the correct one. But: - The 2026.11.7 release notes list only three dependency bumps. The tracking item `pmc-total-item-order` is still `in_progress`, so the generator left it out of the release that shipped it. - Every consumer whose committed CHANGELOG.md has an item with `completed_at` earlier than `closed_at` failed `changelog:check` on its Dependabot pm-toolchain PR (2026.11.6 to 2026.11.7). On 2026-11-11 that was 16 repositories (pm-lint#72, pm-web#315, pm-starter#203, pm-slack#189, pm-brief#214, pm-todos#191, pm-csv#240, pm-jira#200, pm-gantt-chart#223, pm-context#221, pm-hypothesis#27, pm-linear#216, pm-presets#208, pm-graph#206, pm-jev#106, pm-ops#261). The diff is pure reordering, for example in pm-lint: ``` ### Other -- Publish pm-lint as @unbrained/pm-lint (... pm-lint-scoped-npm-name ...) closed 10-30, completed 10-26 - Release readiness behind PM_RELEASE_APPROVED (... pm-lint-release-gate ...) closed 10-27, completed 10-27 +- Publish pm-lint as @unbrained/pm-lint (... pm-lint-scoped-npm-name ...) ``` - The failure message, "Changelog is out of date", reads like the consumer's tracker drifted. Nothing says the generator changed, or that one regeneration fixes it. Verified locally on pm-lint's toolchain branch: pm-changelog 2026.11.6 passes the check against the same SDK (2026.11.7) and the same pm binary, and 2026.11.7 fails it. So the change is in pm-changelog, not in pm-cli. ## Asks 1. Close `pmc-total-item-order` with its delivery evidence (#324, released in 2026.11.7), and record the ordering change for 2026.11.7 as a consumer-visible change with a one-line action: regenerate CHANGELOG.md once. 2. Treat any change to rendered output as a consumer upgrade. Declare it in the consumer-upgrades contract, so `pm-changelog` can say what to do. 3. Make `--check` tell generator drift apart from tracker drift. When the committed file matches what the previous rendering rules would produce from the same tracker, say "the generator's rendering changed in ; run once" instead of only "out of date". The fleet now regenerates these PRs automatically (an hourly sweep on the orchestrator host). Consumers outside the fleet still get a confusing red check on every rendering change. --- ### GitHub comments (1) > **@coderabbitai[bot]** (2026-11-11T05:39:12Z) > > > > >
